security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, React keys, template literals, ANSI terminal text, static URLs, and inline demo media. Real issues remain in the speech input examples, which risk exposing OpenAI keys from client code, and in the stack trace documentation, which recommends eval(code) in a backend route.

remediation.issue: Client-side provider key usage in the speech input example
remediation.suggestion: Move OpenAI transcription calls to a server route and call that route from the client. Keep provider keys in server-only environment variables and document microphone data handling.

remediation.issue: Documentation shows eval(code) in a backend run-code route
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval with a real sandbox, remove the executable example, or clearly mark it unsafe and provide a safe isolated execution pattern.

remediation.issue: Speech input docs do not clearly define the server boundary for external transcription
remediation.suggestion: Update the fallback documentation to show a backend proxy route and avoid placing Authorization headers or provider keys in client examples.

The documentation shows recorded audio being sent directly to OpenAI for transcription. This can be legitimate, but without a clearly server-side boundary it creates privacy and credential-handling risk.

The hardcoded OpenAI transcription endpoint is part of a callback that sends recorded audio to an external service. This is expected functionality, but it needs explicit server-side handling and consent controls.

The snippet places OPENAI_API_KEY into an Authorization header for the transcription request. The example does not clearly keep this code on the server, so copying it into a client path could expose the secret.

The snippet reads process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY for an external API call without documenting a server-only execution boundary. That creates a realistic risk of users exposing the credential in client-side code.
OPENAI_API_KEY is a real secret class and the snippet uses it in an Authorization header. The surrounding fallback example does not clearly direct users to proxy the request through a backend route.

The documentation references an environment-backed OpenAI key in request code for browser speech fallback. It is not direct file access, but it is sensitive credential handling that needs stronger server-only guidance.

The backend route example calls eval(code) on the runCode tool input, which can execute arbitrary JavaScript on the server. This is a direct remote code execution pattern if copied into an application.

The OpenAI API key is used as a bearer token in browser-side code. Public client exposure of a provider API key is a real credential leakage risk.
Although this is not literal environment-file reading, the line exposes an environment-backed OpenAI credential through client-side Authorization logic. The key should stay server-side.

content.user_title: Build AI Chat Interfaces with AI Elements
content.value_statement: AI chat interfaces require many coordinated React components. This skill guides creation and customization of AI Elements components for Vercel AI SDK apps.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to install AI Elements through the AI Elements CLI or shadcn/ui CLI.
Provides guidance for messages, conversations, prompt inputs, tools, sources, speech, and media components.
Shows React and Next.js usage patterns with Vercel AI SDK hooks.
Describes customization through local component files and Tailwind classes.
Includes reference examples for many AI Elements components.
limitations: Requires an existing React or Next.js project for implementation.
Requires compatible shadcn/ui and Tailwind configuration.
Some examples use external services and need secure server-side configuration.
Production apps must adapt examples for security, privacy, and accessibility needs.

use_cases.title: Create Chat UI Components
use_cases.description: Add message, conversation, prompt input, and response components to a Next.js AI application.

use_cases.title: Standardize AI Product Patterns
use_cases.description: Use consistent AI Elements patterns across tools, sources, reasoning, tasks, and media displays.

use_cases.title: Document Component Integration
use_cases.description: Prepare implementation guidance for teams adopting shadcn/ui and Vercel AI SDK together.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Chat View
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AI Elements to add a basic chat view with messages, a conversation container, and a prompt input.

prompt_templates.title: Customize Message Rendering
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an AI Elements message layout that supports user messages, assistant responses, attachments, and action buttons.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Tool Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an AI Elements interface that shows tool calls, tool outputs, sources, and task progress for a coding assistant.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AI Elements implementation for secure API handling, accessible controls, loading states, and consistent shadcn/ui patterns.

output_examples.input: Request to add a simple AI chat interface.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan that identifies the needed AI Elements components and their composition order.

output_examples.input: Request to customize assistant messages with sources and actions.
output: Recommended message structure for assistant responses.
Action placement guidance for copy, retry, and feedback controls.

output_examples.input: Request to prepare a production review.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering server-side API handling, component accessibility, Tailwind setup, and Vercel AI SDK integration points.

best_practices: Keep provider API keys and transcription requests behind server routes.
Follow the existing AI Elements composition patterns before adding new abstractions.
Test components with loading, empty, error, and long-content states.
anti_patterns: Do not place private provider keys in client components or public environment variables.
Do not copy demo data into production without reviewing privacy and security impact.
Do not bypass shadcn/ui and Tailwind conventions with unrelated component patterns.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build AI chat interfaces with AI Elements, React, shadcn/ui, and Vercel AI SDK patterns.

faq.question: Does it install AI Elements automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for using the AI Elements CLI or shadcn/ui CLI.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it include production security guidance?
faq.answer: It includes some guidance, but production apps must keep API keys and external service calls server-side.

faq.question: What project setup is expected?
faq.answer: A React or Next.js project with shadcn/ui, Tailwind, and Vercel AI SDK integration is expected.

faq.question: Can I customize the generated components?
faq.answer: Yes. AI Elements components live in your project and can be customized like local React components.
